subject: Post-call recap — pilot affordability & commit anchors
messages:
From: Sofia Ivanova <sofia.ivanova@redwood.ai>
To: Aditi Shah <aditi@veloxpay.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 10 Sep 2026 15:02:00 -0400
Subject: Post-call recap — pilot affordability & commit anchors

Thanks Aditi — quick recap from our call and proposed next steps. Really helpful conversation; I captured the core pain, goal, and what we think will move the needle.

Pain points (what we heard)
- Token burn is the principal cost driver: conversational flows include long contexts and lots of generation for downstream summarization and NLU.
- Budget ceiling: finance has set an internal cap (~$45k-$60k/month) for initial pilot spend.
- Peak latency and tail spikes during batch settlement windows are causing timeouts for customers.
- Ops bandwidth: small infra team prefers a low-friction pilot with clear rollback.

Business goals
- Validate a production-ready pilot that reduces per-transaction inference cost by 3x (target) while keeping P95 latency <= 250ms for user-facing endpoints.
- Establish repeatable TCO math we can hand to procurement for commit/discount sizing.
- Deliver measurable ROI for a selected set of flows (payments confirmation + refund classification).

High-level TCO levers we discussed
1) Batching + dynamic micro-batches during settlement windows — expected token processing efficiency gains of 20–40% for batch-heavy endpoints.
2) Prefix / KV caching for repeated context (customer metadata + merchant templates) — can reduce generation tokens by ~30–50% on rooted paths.
3) Model footprint changes: 8-bit quantized baseline or a distilled variant for non-critical control paths — compute cost reduction ~30–40%.
4) Routing policy: split reads to a smaller, cheaper model and route complex generation to a larger model; fallbacks to a lower-cost region during non-peak periods.
5) Reserved capacity (Redwood Dedicated) + committed discounts for predictable throughput to reduce unit price during the pilot.

Back-of-envelope example (your numbers + quick assumptions)
- Current: ~1.1M generated tokens / month; list price equivalent ~$0.065/token => ~$71.5k/mo.
- With caching + batching + quantization: we estimate an effective token reduction to ~0.33M tokens equivalent and compute reduction on the remaining to bring monthly cost to ~$22k–$30k depending on commit level — ~2.4–3.2x improvement (conservative range).

Proposed pilot scope & timeline
- Integration sprint: 1–2 weeks (API keys, sample prompts, prefix cache integration).
- Validation & tuning: 3 weeks (batching rules, cache keys, routing policy).
- Load verification: 1–2 weeks (SLA checks, P95 latency, cost telemetry).
- Acceptance criteria: <= $0.03 per effective generated token for pilot flows OR pilot spend <= $45k/month with measured latency SLOs met.

Next steps (asks for VeloxPay)
- Can you confirm the hard cap finance will accept for an initial pilot? You mentioned ~$45k as a preferred cap on the call.
- I attached a first-pass TCO workbook (veloxpay_tco_sheet_v1.xlsx) and the call recording; please review and flag numbers we should adjust.
- Proposed kickoff: Sep 20 — let us know if that fits engineering. If procurement involvement is needed earlier, loop them in.

If you’re comfortable, I’ll send a compact SOW + pilot acceptance criteria doc and a suggested meeting slot for an engineering kickoff.

Thanks again — we’ll keep the pilot lightweight and instrumented so you can see delta metrics quickly.

—
Sofia Ivanova
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
sofia.ivanova@redwood.ai | +1 415-555-0123

Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>, VeloxPay Procurement <procurement@veloxpay.com>
Date: Thu, 10 Sep 2026 16:45:12 -0400
Subject: Re: Post-call recap — pilot affordability & commit anchors

Thanks Sofia — appreciate the clear summary. A few clarifications from our side:

- Budget: Finance is targeting a preferred pilot cap of $45k/month. They might approve up to $60k if we can show a firm path to <$25k within 6 weeks.
- Scope: please make the acceptance criteria explicit — we need a definition for "effective generated token" in the workbook (is that post-cache tokens?).
- Security: our security team will need SOC2 evidence and an outline of data handling (we cannot allow persistent KV caching of PII). Please add a short note on how prefix caching will be implemented with redaction controls.

Procurement (cc) — please advise any standard paperwork or minimum vendor terms we should expect.

Two quick asks: can you add a column in the TCO sheet showing spend under (a) no-change, (b) moderate caching, (c) aggressive caching + quantization? Also share a 1-page pilot acceptance checklist we can circulate to finance/procurement.

On timing — Sep 20 works for our engineering lead (Anil).

—
Aditi Shah
Head of Product, VeloxPay
aditi@veloxpay.com

From: Sofia Ivanova <sofia.ivanova@redwood.ai>
To: Aditi Shah <aditi@veloxpay.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>, VeloxPay Procurement <procurement@veloxpay.com>
Date: Fri, 11 Sep 2026 08:10:05 -0400
Subject: Re: Post-call recap — pilot affordability & commit anchors

Appreciate the notes — answers inline and updated materials attached.

- "Effective generated token" definition: in the workbook the column labeled "net_gen_tokens" is post-cache / de-duped tokens for generation. I added a short doc comment in the sheet and a helper tab that shows calculation steps.
- TCO scenarios: added three columns as requested (no-change / moderate / aggressive) with conservative assumptions: moderate = 35% token reduction via caching + 20% batching efficiency; aggressive = 60% cache + 35% compute reduction via quantization + routing.
- Security & caching: we will not persist PII in any shared cache. Karthik added a note on ephemeral prefix keys and server-side redaction rules; we also support customer-managed KMS for keying any cached entries. I pasted Karthik's snippet below for the security doc: 

"On caching and PII: apply redaction at collection time, store only a hashed context id in the prefix cache, set TTLs <= 24h for any session-level cache; for persisted merchant templates we support encryption-at-rest with customer-managed KMS. Redwood's private deployments can keep caches entirely inside your VPC. SOC2 evidence attached under a secured drive link on request."

- Pilot acceptance checklist (overview) — acceptance criteria we propose:
  * Functionality: expected user flows return correct classifications for 95% of a seed set (we'll share the seed test cases).
  * Cost: pilot flows must show effective per-generated-token cost <= $0.03 OR total pilot spend <= $45k/month.
  * Latency: P95 <= 250ms for user-facing endpoints during normal load.
  * Security: no PII persisted in shared caches; SOC2 evidence reviewed by your security team.

Attached: veloxpay_tco_sheet_v1.xlsx (updated), call_recording_20260910.mp3
Links: HubSpot deal and a drive folder with the improved workbook and pilot checklist: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1a2b3cVeloxPayPilotDocs

Proposed next meeting: Engineering kickoff — Mon Sep 20, 10:00–11:00 PT or Tue Sep 21, 14:00–15:00 PT. Which works for your team?

I will draft a compact SOW & acceptance checklist and circulate before the kickoff.

—
